title: Spectral Gear Engine: Shader Energy Conservation
description: A mechanical skull powered by interlocking gears serves as a spectral energy reactor. The user manipulates custom shader parameters across six energy channels (RGB emissive, fresnel intensity, distortion amplitude, dissolve threshold) distributed between the skull and gears, while maintaining a total energy conservation law. Undo/redo support lets the user backtrack through shader state history.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap/CDN) with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls. Load gears.glb and ScatteringSkull.glb. Position the skull at center, scale gears to mesh around and behind the skull like a mechanical crown/spine apparatus. Use a dark environment with subtle ambient light and one directional light. Camera starts at distance 4 looking at origin. Apply custom ShaderMaterial to both models using onBeforeCompile or RawShaderMaterial. Define 6 shader uniform channels: (1) skull RGB emissive color (3 channels), (2) gear fresnel intensity, (3) skull vertex distortion amplitude, (4) gear dissolve threshold. Implement an ENERGY CONSERVATION LAW: the sum of all 6 normalized channel values (0-1 each) must always equal 3.0. When the user increases one channel, others proportionally decrease to maintain the sum. Create a left-side UI panel with 6 labeled sliders. Each slider adjusts its channel and triggers proportional redistribution across remaining channels. The skull shader should include: emissive glow controlled by RGB channels, vertex displacement using sine-based distortion driven by amplitude uniform, and a pulsing fresnel rim effect. The gear shader should include: a fresnel-based holographic rim controlled by fresnel intensity uniform, a noise-based dissolve effect using dissolve threshold, and slow rotation animation in the vertex shader. Implement full UNDO/REDO: store slider state snapshots in a history stack (max 50). Add Undo (Ctrl+Z) and Redo (Ctrl+Y) keyboard shortcuts plus on-screen buttons. Display current energy total prominently to prove conservation. Add a coupling toggle button: when enabled, adjusting any skull channel mirrors an inverse effect on a paired gear channel. Animate gears rotating slowly. Show step counter tracking total interactions performed.
